item.title: PM says he cannot guarantee they will have the numbers to amend the Constitution
Taveuni resident alleges WAF officer questioned him over speaking to media
item.description: The resident, who has asked not to be named, says the alleged incident happened a few weeks ago when he went with his team to collect water. He alleges a WAF technical officer approached him and asked why he had gone to the media about his concerns.
item.content:encoded:
The resident, who has asked not to be named, says the alleged incident happened a few weeks ago when he went with his team to collect water.

He alleges a WAF technical officer approached him and asked why he had gone to the media about his concerns.

The resident says he told the officer that it was his right to raise his concerns publicly.

He says the officer initially spoke to him in what he describes as a rough manner, but later calmed down and told him that he needed to understand the challenges WAF was facing.

fijivillage News sent questions to WAF regarding the resident's allegations.

WAF says it will look into the matter and provide a response after making the necessary enquiries.

The resident says his broader concern is that people in local communities continue to struggle for water and have to repeatedly contact WAF for assistance.

He also claims he has observed what he believes are quicker water deliveries to some hotels and expatriates, while local residents face delays.

The resident says everyone should be treated fairly and customers with WAF meters should receive proper service.

His latest concerns follow an earlier issue raised with fijivillage News over a $792 payment for 20,000 litres of water.

WAF had explained that the $792 included the cost of the water and transportation to the resident's location, with four 5,000-litre deliveries required.

The resident had said he initially received only 10,000 litres despite paying the full amount and experienced difficulty arranging delivery of the remaining water.

At the time, WAF says its Taveuni team had been waiting for the resident to contact them when he was ready to receive the remaining 10,000 litres.

fijivillage News will update the story once WAF provides a further response following its enquiries into the resident's latest allegations.

item.title: Lateef sentenced to 20 months for meth and marijuana possession
item.description: Former Suva lawyer Shazran Abdul Lateef has been sentenced to 20 months in prison after being convicted of possessing unlawful drugs. He will serve this term concurrently with the three-year, eight-month sentence he is serving for possessing 9.5 grams of methamphetamine and 3.5 grams of marijuana on 9th May 2019.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Mataiciwa urges media to ensure accurate and reliable election reporting
item.description: The media has an important role to play in ensuring voters have access to timely, accurate and reliable information during the electoral process. This has been highlighted by Supervisor of Elections Ana Mataiciwa while opening the Media and Elections Reporting Training at Communications Fiji Limited this morning.
item.content:encoded:
The media has an important role to play in ensuring voters have access to timely, accurate and reliable information during the electoral process.

This has been highlighted by Supervisor of Elections Ana Mataiciwa while opening the Media and Elections Reporting Training at Communications Fiji Limited this morning.

Mataiciwa says the media is one of the most important links between electoral processes and the public, helping voters understand how elections work, what is happening and where they can access verified information.

She says this influence comes with the responsibility to report accurately, fairly and impartially.

Mataiciwa says the training will cover the legal framework governing elections and the media’s role and responsibilities, as well as fact-checking and the growing challenges of misinformation and disinformation, including content generated through artificial intelligence.

She says the programme will also focus on inclusive election reporting, including equitable coverage of women and marginalised candidates and making election information accessible and relevant to Fiji’s diverse voter groups, including young people and those living in rural and maritime communities.

She says a professional and well-informed media is an important partner in ensuring voters have access to credible electoral information.

Mataiciwa says in an environment where information can travel across the country in seconds, misinformation can spread just as quickly, making accuracy more important than ever.
